key_insight: An end-to-end hybrid quantum-classical Benders pipeline can solve MILPs for vehicle routing, but current results suggest quantum speedup is unlikely at the tested problem sizes.
engineering_relevance: This study shows how QAOA-based QUBO solvers can be integrated into industrial optimization workflows, making it relevant for routing and other MILP-driven engineering applications.
method: Benders decomposition with Multiple Cuts via Multiple Solutions (MCMS) to split the MILP.
Quantum-assisted cut selection using gate-based QAOA on tensor-network emulators and superconducting hardware.
Vehicle Routing Problem benchmarked as an end-to-end case study.
evidence_signal: The pipeline was evaluated on 10 permutations of a standard 20-customer, 4-vehicle QOptLib VRP instance with classical cut selection, plus a toy problem using MPS-JuliQAOA for full hybrid assessment.
watch_item: Results are size-dependent: the cut-selection stage was small in classical MCMS runs but dominated runtime in the toy quantum-assisted setup, so the approach is not yet evidence of quantum advantage.
paper_title: Hybrid quantum-classical end-to-end pipeline for solving MILPs: a vehicle routing case study
